what: A verification key DERIVED from Lean-emitted KimchiWrapMain gates is account state on the Mina devnet. Not a key o1js `.compile()` produced — the gate list, coefficients and cross-gate placement come from `Dregg2.Circuit.Emit.KimchiWrapMain`, and `metatheory/fixtures/pickles-vk-derive` encodes them as a `Side_loaded_verification_key.Stable.V2`.

vk.circuit: 498 Lean rows (+15883 Zero pad) -> domain 2^14, public input 6
vk.note: The base64 `data` is deliberately NOT recorded here. Re-checking must RE-DERIVE it, not diff against a copy stored beside the claim; a record that carries the artifact invites verifying the artifact against itself.

derivedFrom.commitNote: HEAD at the moment of derivation. A sibling landed 7411b4241 during the run; it touched TurnAuthGuards, ShieldedRingEndpointDescriptor, lakefile and the orphan gate, and NOTHING on the derivation path, so the key is the same at either commit. The emission fixture was clean against HEAD when read.
derivedFrom.⚑ theHashIsNotStableAcrossCommits: THE DERIVED HASH MOVES WHEN THE LEAN ASSEMBLY MOVES, and it has moved before within a single day. `emissionSha256` is the real anchor: if a future re-derivation disagrees with `vk.hash`, check that sha FIRST. Equal sha + different hash is a derivation bug; different sha means the circuit changed and the chain is simply holding an older key. Neither is 'the chain drifted'.

howItWasAuthorized.authorization: signature (fee payer and target account both signed)
howItWasAuthorized.why: The FIRST key on an account can only go on by signature. `set_verification_key` on a fresh account is `(Signature, Txn_version.current)` (permissions.ml:580-594), and a proof is not merely unnecessary but impossible: the VK that would verify a proof on a VK-setting update is the account's OLD one, explicitly excluding the key being set (zkapp_command.ml:1200-1232), and a virgin account has none.
howItWasAuthorized.cost: 1 MINA account creation fee + 0.1 MINA transaction fee, paid by the fee payer.
howItWasAuthorized.targetWasVirgin: confirmed by reading the account before sending: `account: null`

So 'the stored hash equals ours' is satisfiable by a blob with a label. Re-deriving the digest from the returned bytes is what makes the first two checks mean something.

The verifier discriminates the registered key from its nearest neighbour, so its green is not vacuous.

aProofHasNowBeenProduced.supersedes: `notAWorkingBridge` below said NO PROOF HAS BEEN PRODUCED FOR THIS CIRCUIT. One has: `metatheory/fixtures/pickles-extractors --bin mina_onchain_index_probe` proves the registered emission on Pallas with Mina's SRS and prev_challenges=2.
aProofHasNowBeenProduced.whatMinaSaid: `make_zkapp_verifier_index` fed THESE bytes reconstructs an index whose 28 commitments are identical to the prover's (28/28), and `kimchi::verifier::verify` ACCEPTS the proof at a 40-word public input; at the circuit's own 6 words it returns IncorrectPubicInputLength(40) — "the public input is of an unexpected size (expected 40)".
aProofHasNowBeenProduced.⚠ andWhatItDoesNotMean: the 40-word vector was CHOSEN by the probe (the circuit's 6 words then 34 zeros). Pickles DERIVES all 40 from the statement and lets no prover supply them, so this is a localization of the gap, not a Pickles verification. openmina `verify_zkapp` and o1js `verify` both REFUSE — in the statement, before the key is consulted.

It does NOT mean any proof verifies under it. ⚑ SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-08-05 — see `recheckedOn.aProofHasNowBeenProduced`; a proof now exists and Mina's kimchi verifier accepts it under the index built from these bytes, while Mina's PICKLES verifier still refuses. `KimchiWrapMain` §13 still names eight unassembled sub-circuits; the wrap assembly does not emit them.
⚠ whatThisIsNot.notAContract: This account carries a verification key and nothing else. There is no zkApp method, no state, no deployed logic. It is a key at an address.
⚠ whatThisIsNot.notRelatedToTheAttestedGate: Distinct from `devnet-deployment.json`'s DreggAttestedGate, whose key came from o1js `.compile()` and whose live anchor is SIGNATURE-ONLY (see that file's `sourcesMovedPast`). Nothing here changes that.
⚠ whatThisIsNot.notVerified: The key encodes a circuit; that the circuit is the one Lean specifies rests on the emission path, not on a machine-checked refinement of this artifact. Devnet acceptance is evidence about ENCODING — that the object is a well-formed Side_loaded_verification_key Mina will hold — and about nothing else.
